events.title: William Wallace Is Executed in London
events.description: The Scottish resistance leader William Wallace was tried for treason and put to death at Smithfield in London. He had led Scottish forces against King Edward I of England.
events.significance: Wallace became a lasting symbol of Scottish independence. His death helped turn him into a national martyr and the subject of centuries of legend.

events.title: Birth of Louis XVI of France
events.description: The future King of France was born at Versailles. He took the throne in 1774.
events.significance: Louis XVI was the last king of France before the monarchy was overthrown during the French Revolution. His reign and his execution in 1793 mark a turning point in European history.

events.title: Sacco and Vanzetti Are Executed
events.description: Italian-born anarchists Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti were electrocuted in Massachusetts for murder. Their trial was widely seen as unfair, and the executions set off protests around the world.
events.significance: The case became a lasting symbol of concerns about prejudice and fairness in the justice system. In 1977, Massachusetts Governor Michael Dukakis issued a proclamation honoring their memory.

events.title: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union Sign the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
events.description: In Moscow, the two powers signed a non-aggression treaty. A secret protocol divided Poland, the Baltic states, Finland and Romania into German and Soviet spheres of influence.
events.significance: The pact cleared the way for Germany's invasion of Poland about a week later, which began World War II. It also set the stage for the Soviet takeover of the Baltic states.

events.title: The Baltic Way
events.description: About two million people joined hands in a human chain stretching across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, linking Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius. It took place on the 50th anniversary of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact.
events.significance: This peaceful protest drew the world's attention to the Baltic peoples' demand for freedom from Soviet rule. It became one of the best-known moments of the Singing Revolution.
